construction_notes: Corruption Risk Index (CRI): composite of up to seven red flags -- single bid submitted; non-open procedural type; short advertisement or submission period; no call for tenders published; supplier registered in a tax haven; short decision period; buyer's spending concentration -- built so that a higher value signals higher corruption risk. Table 3 descriptives by country (count / mean / std): Denmark 23,134 / 0.34 / 0.18; Estonia 41,373 / 0.35 / 0.23; Latvia 138,345 / 0.25 / 0.24; Slovakia 63,699 / 0.23 / 0.21; Ukraine 1,254,401 / 0.27 / 0.32; UK 126,282 / 0.38 / 0.22; min 0 and max 1 in every country.
BO data aggregated from individual to company level; for numerical variables the minimum or maximum across the company's owners was used.
Company frequency by BO: the highest value among the company's owners taken as the aggregate company value (Table 4 means: DK 14, EE 5, LV 3, SK 2, UA 7, UK 4; maxima 202, 311, 122, 16, 495, 1324).
Foreign BO: a company is flagged risky whenever at least one of its BOs is a foreigner relative to the tendering country (Table 7 counts by category).
Sanctioned-country BO: at least one BO from Russia, Belarus or Iran (Table 7: 0 in Denmark and Estonia, 189 Latvia, 924 Slovakia, 4296 Ukraine, 184 UK).
BO age: computed from BO dates of birth, available only for Latvia, Slovakia and the UK; both the oldest and the youngest BO of a company were used (Table 6 means 58 / 54 / 54 years).
BO information change frequency: calculable only for Denmark and Estonia (Table 5 max 11 and 7 changes).

Company age: calculable only for Denmark and Slovakia (Table 8: DK mean 19, max 90; SK mean 15, min -4 because the Slovak BO data record the entry date to the electronic register, which can post-date company registration).

No BO data: operationalised as the lack of matched BO-procurement data after removing sole entrepreneurs and joint-stock companies without BO requirements; in Ukraine and the UK the register's own 'unable to identify or locate a BO' notification is used instead.

Variables of interest and control factors with relatively high missing rates are transformed into deciles with an additional missing category, so that all observations are retained and non-linear threshold effects can be traced.
Table 11 reports the pooled prevalence of each validated risk flag among contracts, e.g. company frequency by BO: Denmark 4.0%, Estonia 13.8%, Latvia 7.7%, Ukraine 12.3%, UK 1.6%.

links.pointer_quote: We find that BO-based risk indicators capturing unusual and outlier BO features - high company frequency of BO, frequent information change, outlier BO age, and no BO data - all perform in line with expected results.

claims.statement: In UK, public procurement contracts whose winning supplier is flagged by the BO-risk indicator 'Number of companies owned by the same beneficial owner' in the category top decile of max_bo_freq: 9-1324 companies owned by the same BO have a higher Corruption Risk Index than contracts in the reference category, conditional on tender year, product market, tender price, buyer type and buyer location.

register_source.value: People with significant control register (PSC) (UK beneficial ownership register), matched to opentender.eu public procurement data

definition.value: Number of companies owned by the same natural person, taken from the national BO register and aggregated from the individual to the company level by taking the highest value among the company's owners ('max_bo_freq'); the continuous distribution is sliced into deciles with an additional missing category and entered as category dummies, the risky category being the top of the distribution.

register_source.value: opentender.eu public procurement data

definition.value: Composite public procurement corruption risk indicator (Fazekas & Kocsis, 2020) computed on the awarded contract from up to seven 'red flags': (1) single bid submitted in a tender; (2) non-open procedural type; (3) short advertisement or submission period; (4) no call for tenders published; (5) supplier registered in a tax haven; (6) short decision period; and (7) buyer's spending concentration. Constructed so that a higher value signals a higher risk of corruption; it runs from 0 to 1 (Table 3 min 0, max 1).

timing.value: measured on the public procurement contract/tender itself, at award

units.value: change in the Corruption Risk Index relative to the reference category, in CRI index points (CRI runs 0-1)

magnitude.interpretation: a distinct jump in procurement risks at the top decile of the indicator

estimand.target_population: public procurement contracts awarded in UK in 2016-2021 whose winning supplier could be matched to the People with significant control register (PSC)

population.description: UK: contract-level matched public procurement x beneficial-ownership dataset, matched years 2016-2021. Table 2 reports 8,317,840 companies in the BO register, 126,282 bid IDs and 40,045 bids with BOs (31.7%); Table 3 reports 126,282 contracts with a CRI value.
subgroups_defined: deciles (or bins) of the continuous BO risk indicator, plus a separate missing category
population.selection: contracts without bidder names removed; foreign bidders removed where the national BO register covers domestic companies only (Denmark, Estonia, Latvia, UK); publicly listed joint-stock companies removed because they need not file BO data; procurement data filtered from the year the BO register started operating, except for Denmark and Slovakia whose BO data are historical; Ukraine additionally drops individual entrepreneurs and bids below 250,000 UAH; Slovakia drops contracts below EUR 100,000

identification.source_of_variation: cross-sectional variation across public procurement contracts within the same tender year, 2-digit CPV product market, tender price band, buyer type and buyer location, estimated separately for each country; no reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument is used -- the paper frames the estimates as conditional correlations used for convergent validity testing

key_assumptions.assumption: Convergent validity: a conditional correlation between a newly proposed BO-based company risk indicator and the already validated public procurement Corruption Risk Index is read as evidence that the BO indicator measures corruption.
key_assumptions.supported_by: content validation of each indicator against the paper's definition of corruption (Theoretical Framework section) and documented corruption cases in Annex F

key_assumptions.assumption: Both indicator sets are noisy proxies of the same unobserved, deliberately hidden corruption phenomenon; there is no 'true' measure of the underlying concept, so a low correlation need not mean a lack of validity.
key_assumptions.supported_by: stated as a limitation of convergent validation in the introduction

threats_discussed: both the established (CRI) and the new (BO) indicators are noisy, so a low correlation may not mean a lack of validity

limited coverage of bidder/supplier ID codes in the procurement data lowers matching accuracy, especially in the UK
